title: Artin--Rees principal-quotient colength difference
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak a)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $0\ne x\in\mathfrak a$, and put $B=A/xA$, a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak a B$. For $n\ge1$ put $H_A(n)=\mathrm{length}_A(A/\mathfrak a^n)$ and $H_B(n)=\mathrm{length}_B(B/\mathfrak b^n)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and assume these lengths are finite. There is an integer $c\ge1$ such that for every integer $n>c$,
$$xA\cap\mathfrak a^n\subseteq\mathfrak a^{n-c}xA,$$
$$H_B(n)=H_A(n)-\mathrm{length}_A\bigl(xA/(xA\cap\mathfrak a^n)\bigr)\le H_A(n)-H_A(n-c).$$
Here the middle quotient has finite length, and the $A$-length of $B/\mathfrak b^n=A/(xA+\mathfrak a^n)$ equals its $B$-length.

source.place: Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees, applied to xA inside A; explicit local-domain colength specialization of its intersection bound and the short exact quotient sequence used in the proof of Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $R=A$, $I=\mathfrak a$, $M=A$ and $N=xA$. The module $A$ is generated by $1$ (and $xA$ by $x$). Obtain $c_0\ge0$, and take $c=\max(1,c_0)$. Its enlarged-constant inclusion gives $J_n:=xA\cap\mathfrak a^n\subseteq\mathfrak a^{n-c}xA$ for every $n>c$. This is the first assertion, with one constant independent of $n$.

source.place: Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees, inclusion and enlargement of the constant.

proof.text: Fix $n>c$. The quotient map $A\to B$ carries $\mathfrak a^n$ onto $\mathfrak b^n$: both are generated by products of $n$ images of elements of $\mathfrak a$. Its composite with $B\to B/\mathfrak b^n$ therefore gives the identification $Q_n:=A/(xA+\mathfrak a^n)\cong B/\mathfrak b^n$. Every $A$-submodule $U$ of this $B$-module is a $B$-submodule: for $b\in B$, choose a lift $a\in A$, so $bu=au\in U$. The converse is immediate. The strict submodule chains are identical, hence [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives $\mathrm{length}_A(Q_n)=\mathrm{length}_B(B/\mathfrak b^n)=H_B(n)$.

source.place: Tag 00IX, lemma-length-independent, its two-line filtration proof; quotient map calculated explicitly.

proof.text: The maps $xA/J_n\to A/\mathfrak a^n$, $u+J_n\mapsto u+\mathfrak a^n$, and $A/\mathfrak a^n\to Q_n$, $a+\mathfrak a^n\mapsto a+(xA+\mathfrak a^n)$, are linear. The first is injective since its kernel is $(xA\cap\mathfrak a^n)/J_n=0$; the second is surjective, and its kernel consists exactly of the images of elements of $xA$. Thus they form a short exact sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], $H_A(n)=\mathrm{length}_A(xA/J_n)+\mathrm{length}_A(Q_n)$. Finiteness of $H_A(n)$ makes both summands finite. Step 2 identifies the second summand with $H_B(n)$, giving the asserted difference equality.

source.place: Tag 00K6, lemma-hilbert-ses, proof: the displayed short exact quotient sequence; Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive.

proof.text: Put $r=n-c\ge1$. Multiplication induces an $A$-linear bijection $A/\mathfrak a^r\to xA/\mathfrak a^r xA$, $a+\mathfrak a^r\mapsto xa+\mathfrak a^r xA$. It is well defined and surjective; if $xa\in\mathfrak a^r xA=x\mathfrak a^r$, write $xa=xb$ with $b\in\mathfrak a^r$. Since $x\ne0$ and $A$ is a domain, $a=b$. This proves injectivity. A linear bijection and its inverse carry submodule chains bijectively to submodule chains, preserving strictness. Consequently [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives $\mathrm{length}_A(xA/\mathfrak a^r xA)=H_A(r)$.

source.place: Tag 02LY, definition-length; multiplication-by-x identification in the domain specialization of Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: By Step 1, the map $xA/J_n\to xA/\mathfrak a^r xA$ sending the class of $u$ to the class of the same $u$ is well defined and surjective. Its kernel is $\mathfrak a^r xA/J_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the resulting short exact sequence. Its middle module has finite length by Step 3, so all lengths are finite and $\mathrm{length}_A(xA/J_n)=\mathrm{length}_A(\mathfrak a^r xA/J_n)+H_A(r)\ge H_A(r)$, using Step 4.

source.place: Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive, applied to the quotient map induced by the Artin--Rees inclusion.

proof.text: Combining Steps 3 and 5 and subtracting finite integers yields $H_B(n)=H_A(n)-\mathrm{length}_A(xA/J_n)\le H_A(n)-H_A(n-c)$. Step 3 also ensures that the subtracted length is at most $H_A(n)$, so no infinite or negative subtraction is involved. This holds for every $n>c$, with the constant fixed in Step 1.

source.place: Elementary finite-integer arithmetic after Tags 00IN and 00IV.
